conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. You're in the ICU now. We're taking care of you for diabetic ketoacidosis. Can you tell me how you’ve been feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been really sick. Nauseous, throwing up, and this awful pain in my upper belly. It’s like my pancreas is on fire.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. Your labs show you were in DKA—diabetic ketoacidosis. That means your blood sugar was very high and your body was making ketones. We’ve started fluids and insulin to fix that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know I missed some insulin. I just couldn’t keep up. But the pain—it’s not always from DKA, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're right. Your pain is likely related to your chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic issues. But right now, the DKA is the main problem. We’ll manage your pain too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had this before. Eight weeks ago. It keeps coming back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and we see your history. You have pancreatic divisum and scarring, which makes you prone to this. But today, the DKA is what brought you in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Am I going to be okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re responding well. Your blood sugar is coming down, and you’re getting better. We’ll keep you in the ICU tonight, then move you to the regular floor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs improved overnight. Blood sugar is 292, anion gap is closing. We’re stopping the insulin drip soon and switching to shots.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Shots? I was on U500 at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but we’re switching to U100 Regular insulin because it’s easier to get at pharmacies. You know how to use both, so we’ll go with what’s available.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I guess that’s fine. But I need my pain meds. I’m hurting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re continuing your Dilaudid 6mg every 3 hours as needed. You can take it now if you’d like.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please. The pain is bad.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re transferring you to the medicine floor this afternoon. Your vitals are stable, and you’re tolerating food.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. But where will I go after? I don’t have a place right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re working on that. Social work found temporary housing for you. You’ll have a place to go when you’re discharged.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ve been so stressed about that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. Your blood sugar is 180 this morning—much better. We’re keeping you on the new insulin schedule. Any nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little, but not like before. The prochlorperazine helps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep it as needed. Your lipase was normal, so no sign of acute pancreatitis this time—just the chronic pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So the pain isn’t from a flare-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not this time. It’s likely from your chronic condition and the DKA. As your body recovers, the pain should ease.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your A1c came back—it’s 11.6%. That means your diabetes has been poorly controlled over the last few months.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know. I try, but sometimes I just can’t do it all.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re not judging. We want to help. Diabetes education will talk to you today about ways to make it easier.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’ll listen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing great. Blood sugar is steady, and you’ve had no vomiting. We’re planning to discharge you in a day or two.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. But what about my meds? I lost everything when I left my last place.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you a 7-day supply of all your medications when you leave. That’ll give you time to get them refilled.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. And the insulin? Will I go back to U500?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You can use U100 for now. If you need U500 later, your doctor can help, but U100 is what’s available in most pharmacies.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All your labs are normal now. Blood sugar is 130, no ketones. You’re almost ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. But I’m scared I’ll end up back here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We are too. That’s why we’re stressing follow-up. You’ll see your PCP soon, and we’ll help connect you with support.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I have a guardian. She helps me make decisions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ve spoken with her. She supports your care plan, so we can move forward safely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today’s the day. We’re finalizing your discharge. You’ve done really well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel so much better. No pain, not nauseous.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll send you home with your meds, instructions, and follow-up appointments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I see a specialist for my pancreas?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re scheduled to follow up with gastroenterology. They’ll manage your chronic pancreatitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my mental health? I’ve been struggling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll follow up with your behavioral health provider. We know this is hard, and support is available.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Final check before discharge. You’re alert, pain-free, and labs are stable. Ready to go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Thank you for helping me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Remember—take your insulin, manage your diet, and call if you’re not feeling well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I don’t want to come back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll do everything we can to help you stay healthy. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick update—your discharge papers are ready. You’ll get a ride to your new housing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I was worried about that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve got it covered. And remember—your PCP appointment is in three days. Please go.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll be there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your urine test showed benzodiazepines, but no other drugs. Just want to make sure you’re safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I take diazepam for anxiety. It’s prescribed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s on your list. Just confirming. All good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you for checking.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re discharging you soon. Any last questions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I think I’m good. Just ready to rest at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve earned it. Take care of yourself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The transport is here. You’re all set.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll remember that.
